title: LNbits rushes emergency patch after reported Bitcoin wallet thefts
summary: The project warned that installations running older versions were vulnerable and urged operators to replace potentially exposed credentials even after upgrading.
content: LNbits has rushed out an emergency software patch following reports of Bitcoin wallet thefts. The development team warned that any installations running older versions remain vulnerable to attacks. Operators have been strongly urged to immediately upgrade their systems and replace any potentially exposed credentials to secure their funds, even after the update process is completed.
content_ta: Bitcoin wallet திருட்டுகள் குறித்த புகார்களைத் தொடர்ந்து, LNbits நிறுவனம் அவசர மென்பொருள் திருத்தத்தை (patch) வெளியிட்டுள்ளது. பழைய பதிப்புகளைப் பயன்படுத்தும் அமைப்புகள் தாக்குதல்களுக்கு உள்ளாக வாய்ப்புள்ளதாக டெவலப்பர்கள் எச்சரித்துள்ளனர். கணினிகளை உடனடியாக மேம்படுத்துவதுடன், பாதிக்கப்படக்கூடிய சான்றுகளையும் (credentials) மாற்றும்படி ஆபரேட்டர்கள் கேட்டுக் கொள்ளப்பட்டுள்ளனர்.

title: Philippines SEC confirms data breach as BIR investigates 340K record leak claims
summary: Names, addresses, contact details, and taxpayer identification numbers may have been exposed but...
content: The Philippines SEC has confirmed a data breach following claims that 340,000 records were leaked. The BIR is currently investigating the incident, which potentially exposed sensitive information including names, addresses, contact details, and taxpayer identification numbers. Authorities are working to assess the full extent and impact of the exposure.
content_ta: Philippines SEC-ல் தரவு திருட்டு உறுதி செய்யப்பட்டுள்ளது. 340,000 பதிவுகள் கசிந்ததாகக் கூறப்படும் குற்றச்சாட்டுகளைத் தொடர்ந்து BIR விசாரணை நடத்தி வருகிறது. பெயர்கள், முகவரிகள், தொடர்பு எண்கள் மற்றும் வரி செலுத்துவோர் அடையாள எண்கள் வெளிப்பட்டிருக்கலாம் என்று அஞ்சப்படுகிறது.

title: Initia confirms second exploit in 3 weeks, $3.27M stolen in latest attack
summary: Initia said an attacker exploited compromised cloud credentials to move $3.27 million in crypto assets, with about $2.16 million remaining frozen on its halted network.
content: Initia has confirmed a second security exploit within three weeks, resulting in the theft of $3.27 million in crypto assets. The attacker reportedly utilized compromised cloud credentials to carry out the attack. Following the incident, the network was halted, leaving approximately $2.16 million of the stolen funds frozen.
content_ta: Initia நெட்வொர்க்கில் மூன்று வாரங்களுக்குள் இரண்டாவது முறையாக பாதுகாப்பு மீறல் ஏற்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்த சமீபத்தைய சைபர் தாக்குதலில் $3.27 மில்லியன் மதிப்பிலான கிரிப்டோ சொத்துக்கள் திருடப்பட்டுள்ளதாக நிறுவனம் உறுதிப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. சமரசம் செய்யப்பட்ட கிளவுட் சான்றுகளைப் (cloud credentials) பயன்படுத்தி இந்தத் தாக்குதல் நடத்தப்பட்டுள்ளது. இந்தச் சம்பவத்தைத் தொடர்ந்து நெட்வொர்க் தற்காலிகமாக நிறுத்தப்பட்ட நிலையில், மீதமுள்ள $2.16 மில்லியன் மதிப்புள்ள நிதிகள் முடக்கப்பட்டுள்ளன.

title: Across Protocol restores website after hackers hijack domain
summary: The cross-chain bridge said a social engineering attack targeting domain registrar Namecheap allowed hackers to redirect users to a phishing site.
content: Across Protocol successfully restored its website after hackers hijacked the domain in a cyberattack. The cross-chain bridge revealed that the incident was caused by a social engineering attack targeting their domain registrar, Namecheap. This security breach allowed unauthorized actors to redirect unsuspecting users to a malicious phishing site. The platform acted quickly to resolve the issue and secure its online presence.
content_ta: Across Protocol தனது இணையதளத்தை ஹேக்கர்கள் முடக்கியதை தொடர்ந்து வெற்றிகரமாக மீட்டது. Namecheap டொமைன் பதிவாளரை குறிவைத்து நடத்தப்பட்ட சமூகப் பொறியியல் தாக்குதலே இதற்குக் காரணம் என்று இந்த கிராஸ்-செயின் பிரிட்ஜ் தெரிவித்தது. இந்த பாதுகாப்பு மீறல் மூலம் பயனர்கள் ஒரு ஃபிஷிங் வலைத்தளத்திற்கு திசைதிருப்பப்பட்டனர். சிக்கலைத் தீர்க்கவும் தனது இணையதளப் பாதுகாப்பை உறுதிப்படுத்தவும் நிறுவனம் உடனடியாக நடவடிக்கை எடுத்தது.

title: Adyen Research Finds 72% of Young Shoppers Trust AI to Buy on Their Behalf, but Big-Ticket Purchases Lag
summary:
Adyen, the global financial technology platform of choice for leading businesses, today published new consumer research examining how global shopping behaviors have evolved over the past 20 years, and where commerce is headed next. Marking the company’s 20th year of solving payment complexity, the study benchmarks shifting expectations across the retail landscape. 
A major highlight is the rise of agentic commerce. As AI evolves into an automated buyer, consumers are increasingly open to delegating routine, low-risk purchases, while retaining manual control over higher-value transactions.
Outsourcing the Essentials
The research shows that shoppers are most comfortable using AI to handle routine errands. Across all age groups, standard weekly groceries (18%) and household essentials like laundry detergent (15%) are the top categories shoppers would allow an AI assistant to purchase automatically, without seeking prior approval. This is followed closely by regular takeout food orders (17%) and routine pet supplies (15%).
Drawing the Line at Luxury
Trust in AI drops significantly as the stakes, and price tags, rise. In the UK, only 12% of shoppers are comfortable letting AI book flights, hotels, or holidays, and just 9% would allow automatic purchases of luxury goods.
Yet, younger shoppers remain the early adopters even in high-value categories: more than 1 in 5 (23%) twenty-somethings are happy to let an assistant book their travel, and 18% would trust AI to automatically buy designer apparel and homeware.
The Generational Divide
The appetite for automated spending reveals an extreme generational gap. While nearly 74% of shoppers over 70 refuse to let AI buy on their behalf, digital-native demographics are actively embracing the shift. Among 20-29 year olds, 25% are ready to automate their grocery shopping, 23% are comfortable automating household essentials, and 24% trust AI assistants to order their takeout.
"Over the last twenty years, we've helped merchants navigate every major shift in commerce," commented Karan Katyal, Global Head of Agentic Commerce at Adyen. "Consumers are starting to treat AI as a digital personal assistant, but trust must be built from the ground up. For enterprises, seamless payment infrastructure is key to capturing agentic commerce as that trust grows."

title: Cribl Acquires Tero to Lead Observability Into the AI Era
summary:
Cribl, the AI Platform for Telemetry, today announced it has acquired Tero, which builds an intelligence layer for observability data. Tero co-founders Ben Johnson (CEO), Adam Cohen (CTO), and Nihar Singhal (COO) join Cribl with their team of engineers to help lead its observability roadmap. Johnson previously co-founded Timber, which created the open source Vector observability pipeline and was acquired by Datadog in 2021.
“The best builders in observability are choosing to build with Cribl,” said Clint Sharp, co-founder and CEO of Cribl. “Ben has spent a decade on the hardest problem in this space: helping engineers control their data and know which of it actually matters. Now he and his team will help us take the next step, building observability directly on the platform our customers already trust with their data, for engineers and the AI agents working alongside them.”
Tero built technology that measures how much of an organisation’s telemetry is waste, pinpoints low-value data across observability tools, and lets engineers fix it in the tools they already use. At Cribl, the team will help lead the roadmap across host monitoring, application performance monitoring (APM), federated observability, and AI-native observability, bringing those capabilities onto the same open platform customers already use to collect, route, and optimise their telemetry.
“We started Tero to help engineers understand their telemetry, not just collect more of it. Watching what Cribl was shipping, it became clear we could either compete with them or build it together,” said Johnson, VP of Observability at Cribl. “Cribl has the platform, the customers, and the momentum to define how observability works in the age of AI. That’s where I want to be building.”
Tero is Cribl’s third acquisition in four months, following CardinalOps in July and Radiant Security’s AI SOC technology in August. The Tero deal brings Cribl a team with deep knowledge of the market, credibility with customers and partners, and the experience to accelerate product development. Together, these acquisitions extend Cribl’s market toward first-party observability and security capabilities on a single open telemetry platform.
Read more from Ben Johnson on why he joined Cribl on the Cribl blog, or visit the Cribl booth #205 at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City.

title: Airbnb API: Perk Becomes First to Integrate It for Work Travel
summary:
Perk, the AI-native platform for travel and spend management, will announce a partnership with Airbnb that makes it the first to integrate Airbnb’s API for work travel. Travelers will be able to search and book Airbnb stays with live pricing and availability alongside the rest of their work trips, without leaving Perk.
What it means for employees and finance teams
People traveling for work can now browse live Airbnb listings directly in Perk's Stays tab, and filter results by live availability and pricing. Once a booking is accepted, travelers can view and manage their Airbnb stay on Perk.
For finance teams, Airbnb stays now come with the same travel policy control and expense visibility as flights, hotels and rail. That means no manual reconciliation across platforms.
The demand was already there
Until now, Perk customers booked Airbnb listings manually through the Perk concierge service. Even so, Airbnb nights booked on Perk are up 94% in two years.
Airbnb stays booked through Perk average 9 nights, more than four times the length of a typical hotel booking.
Since January 2024, 78% of Perk’s Airbnb bookings have been for entire homes or apartments, rather than individual rooms.
The companies driving this growth are mostly mid-market to large organizations, led by Professional Services and Manufacturing, whose employees travel for project-based work such as field assignments and long-term client engagements.
“Our customers have been looking for Airbnb stays, especially for longer, project-based trips, and our booking data shows it. So we’ve brought Airbnb listings inside Perk, right where they already book work travel. Travelers can book the stay that fits the trip, and finance teams keep full control, so nobody has to choose between the two,” said Nikita Miller, President of Product and Technology at Perk.

title: Wirex Strengthens UK Board With Appointment of Julian Sawyer as Independent Non-Executive Director
summary:
Wirex Limited, the UK headquartered payments provider, has appointed Julian Sawyer, co-founder and former Chief Operating Officer of Starling Bank, to the Board as an Independent Non-Executive Director.

Sawyer co-founded Starling Bank in 2015 and served as its Chief Operating Officer until 2019, leading the bank’s operations, including its card launch and Starling Payment Services, its platform giving other firms access to UK payment schemes. He went on to become Managing Director, Europe at Gemini, and then Chief Executive Officer of Bitstamp and Zodia Custody, and is an Independent Non-Executive Director of Recognise Bank. 
Chetan Shah, CEO of Wirex Limited, said: “I’m delighted to welcome Julian to the Board of Wirex Limited. title: Wise Expands U.S. Product Suite, Giving Customers New Ways to Earn Returns
summary:
Wise, the global technology company building the best way to move and manage the world's money, today announced an expansion of its US product offering, giving people and businesses two new ways to earn a return on the money they hold with Wise.
The expansion introduces Wise Interest and Stocks, two new products available directly from customers' existing USD balance. Unlike traditional alternatives that require customers to move or lock away their money to earn a return, customers who opt in to these products keep instant access to their funds, meaning they can continue to send and spend from the same balance with no withdrawal penalties. Wise Interest and Stocks are offered by Wise US Assets Inc., a registered broker-dealer. Member of SIPC, which protects securities customers of its members up to $500,000 (including $250,000 for claims for cash). 
Vinay Nilakantan, Head of Product for North America at Wise, said: "People and businesses around the world are keeping more money with Wise than ever. Global customer holdings grew 40% to $39 billion last financial year alone. Now, we want to offer Wise customers more ways to put that money to work, without compromising the convenience and flexibility they expect from us.
"In the US, earning a competitive return too often means locking your money away or juggling multiple accounts. But with Wise Interest and Stocks, people and businesses in the US no longer have to choose between making their money work harder and actually being able to use it. They have the freedom to do both."
Introducing new ways for Wise customers to earn a return
Wise Interest allows customers to earn a return on USD held with Wise through a money market fund holding government-backed assets. Customers' money remains instantly available to send and spend within the same balance, offering greater convenience and flexibility. Returns, which are not guaranteed, are calculated daily and paid into customers' accounts monthly, and over 90% of returns earned may also be exempt from state and local income taxes.
For customers looking for potential longer-term returns, Stocks gives people and businesses a simple way to invest money held with Wise in an S&P 500 index fund. This lets them invest across a diverse range of leading US companies while keeping a high degree of liquidity. Investing involves risk, including possible loss of principal. Wise Interest seeks to preserve the value of an investment, but the investment value of Stocks will change with the market.
Customers can start using either product directly from their existing USD balances by simply selecting Wise Interest or Stocks. In line with Wise's commitment to transparency and low costs, customers will see the fees associated with each product clearly before opting in.
Expanding Wise's existing US product suite
The launch comes as customers increasingly use Wise to hold more of their money and look for more ways to grow those funds. Income earned by US customers through Wise's existing Basic Interest offering, which allows customers in the US to receive interest on USD, GBP and EUR, increased by almost 17% year over year in FY26. Basic Interest is an opt-in feature that allows customers to earn interest on eligible balances held in a Wise account with Wise US Inc. Customer funds are held at Wise US Inc.'s program bank, which pays interest on those funds, and a portion of that interest is passed through to eligible customers.
Wise Interest and Stocks build on the range of existing products already available to Wise personal and business customers in the US. Today, customers can hold and convert more than 40 currencies, get paid in nine currencies using local account details, send money internationally with 77% of payments arriving instantly (in under 20 seconds), and spend around the world with the Wise Multi-Currency Card.
The launch of Wise Interest and Stocks marks the first time Wise has operationalized its US broker-dealer license, which it holds in all 50 states, to offer more tailored products to local customers.

title: Zilch Expands Debt Facilities to £395 Million
summary:
Zilch, the consumer payments app, today announces the successful expansion of its securitisation and corporate debt facilities by an additional £165 million in aggregate. This takes the total commitment available to £395 million, supporting high demand for its evolving product suite. This latest round was led by Deutsche Bank and includes participation from two of the world’s largest credit funds. 
The expanded facilities will enable Zilch to originate up to £6 billion in lending annually, providing additional capacity to support continued customer growth and demand for its newer products. This includes Zilch’s longer-dated Pay Monthly product, launched in August 2026, which allows qualifying customers to spread the cost of purchases over 3, 6 or 12 months. It gives customers greater flexibility to spread the cost of larger purchases, including holidays, household appliances and insurance premiums, providing an alternative to high-interest credit cards or personal loans and enabling Zilch to serve a broader range of purchasing needs. 
Average annual spend per active customer has reached £2,500 and the GMV run rate has passed £3.5bn, which shows Zilch is becoming a default part of how its customers pay for everyday purchases. 
Philip Belamant, CEO and Co-Founder of Zilch, said: “As we continue to grow at significant scale, having access to efficient funding is a key parameter for success. These expanded facilities give us greater capacity to support our customers where they need us, capturing more of the transactions that matter to customers day to day and providing the most rewarding ways to pay. By serving a broader range of customer needs, we can continue building a highly engaged customer relationship and delivering the value, flexibility and features that our customers really want.” 
Hugh Courtney, Chief Financial Officer of Zilch, said: “We are proud of our close partnerships with our funders, led by Deutsche Bank, who continue to support our growth as we scale the business profitably in the UK. The upsizing of the facilities represents a strong endorsement of our underwriting capabilities, product market fit and ability to continue scaling at pace.”  
 


The expansion of the facilities comes off the back of an impressive period of growth for Zilch, which recently announced that it had surpassed a $300m annual run rate and delivered two consecutive quarters of adjusted profit before tax in FY27. It also recently announced plans to move to a new London HQ in Spring 2027, more than doubling office capacity.

title: FI Works Launches Signals to Turn Predictive Insights Into Action for Community Banks and Credit Unions
summary:
FI Works, the Relationship Intelligence and Engagement Platform purpose-built for community banks and credit unions, today announced Signals, a new feature that uses machine learning to identify households likely to add a product, adopt checking or digital services, or leave the institution. Because Signals runs inside the same platform as FI Works' marketing automation and CRM, teams can move from a signal to a targeted campaign, an opportunity, or a frontline follow-up task without exporting a list or switching systems.
Community institutions are increasingly investing in tools that promise to spot opportunities in their data. However, many of those tools rely primarily on transaction data, which reveals only a narrow slice of a relationship. By the time a payment to another lender appears in the transaction feed, the customer or member has often moved the business already. Signals is the industry's solution to this.
"Institutions that bought signal tools in the past tell us the results feel like a 'so what,'" said Keith Henkel, founder and CEO of FI Works. "Most of those tools point to opportunities you've already lost. FI Works Signals casts a much wider net across everything an institution knows about its relationships, and it lets a team go straight from a signal into a campaign in seconds. No one needs to be a data scientist to use the results."
Signals analyzes an institution's integrated data, not transactions alone, to uncover opportunities to grow loans and deposits, increase service adoption, and retain valuable relationships. Predictive scores help financial institutions prioritize outreach, while predicted balances and profitability show the potential value of each opportunity. Because Signals looks for early warning signs, an attrition signal can prompt a conversation before the customer or member starts moving money. Connected reporting helps teams track outcomes and refine their approach.
"Finding the opportunity is only half the job," Henkel said. "Banks and credit unions need to know whom to contact, why, and what that relationship could be worth, and then they need a way to act on it. Signals puts discovery and action in the same place, which is where community institutions have always needed them."

title: Bank of England’s Cautious Interest Rate Rise Could Prolong High Borrowing Costs, Warns NIESR
summary:
The Bank of England’s measured response to rising prices risks keeping interest rates higher for longer than necessary according to The National Institute of Economic and Social Research.
Last week the Monetary Policy Committee raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% and signalled that a further increase may follow. Niesr has argued this approach is too tentative and could leave inflation above the 2% target until at least 2030, making higher prices a lasting feature of the UK economy.
UK inflation is currently 3.5%, driven mainly by fuel costs. Niesr expects it to pass 4% in the new year, just as many 2027 pay settlements are being negotiated, which raises the risk of price rises becoming entrenched in wages.
Oil and gas costs have climbed steeply since the US and Israel began military action against Iran in late February. Brent crude, which traded around $70 a barrel before the conflict, has recently stayed above $100. It briefly dipped below $90 on Tuesday, its lowest level since 31 August, after President Trump played down the need for military action.
Sachin Agrawal, Managing Director for Zoho UK, commented: “UK businesses are being squeezed in every direction, and persistent inflation and the potential of higher interest rates for longer are placing real pressure on businesses, particularly as they finalise budgets ahead of the new year. That makes confidence and clarity all the more important and businesses will want to see a credible path back to stable prices.”
“AI has a vital role to play in helping businesses navigate this by driving growth for both businesses and the wider economy and helping firms boost productivity as costs rise. Where that sits is important, building sovereign infrastructure to keep UK data and AI under UK jurisdictions and giving businesses greater control over how their data is stored and used.”
“The government is responsible for supporting businesses through the rough patch they're currently facing, and with public finances under pressure, deferring difficult decisions only adds to uncertainty. Policymakers need to prioritise policies that empower businesses and support investment in digital capability.”
Niesr also criticised last month’s Budget, in which Chancellor John Healey was accused of postponing difficult choices. The institute estimates that repeating the past decade’s pattern of deferral would leave a £30bn gap in the public finances next year. 
David Aikman, Director of Nieser cautioned that markets could push up UK borrowing costs if defence and other spending rises are not matched by savings elsewhere.

title: Equifax UK and ClearScore Harness Rental Data to Help Drive Financial Inclusion for Millions of Renters
summary:
Credit reference agency Equifax UK and ClearScore have deepened their 10-year partnership through a new initiative to integrate rental payment data directly into Equifax credit files. By incorporating regular rent payments, the initiative can help improve access to credit for millions of tenants. In particular, it supports renters who have little to no traditional borrowing history, turning their single largest monthly commitment into proof of financial reliability.
Through the ClearScore app, renters will be able to securely connect their bank account via open banking to verify ongoing rental payments, free of charge. Crédit Agricole Deutschland marks the next stage of the Group’s growth in Germany, building on more than 70 years in the country and the one million customers its businesses already serve. Following standout partnerships with global names such as Porsche and Giesecke+Devrient (G+D), it cements Enfuce’s positioning as a reliable partner for scalable card programmes across European banking and corporate sectors. 
The launch also broadens the choice of digital banking and payment services available to German consumers. In a market where cash remains an important part of everyday payments, Crédit Agricole Deutschland and Enfuce are making secure, app-based card payments part of the banking experience from day one.
Denise Johansson, CEO and Co-founder of Enfuce, said: “Together with Crédit Agricole Deutschland, we’re here to set a new standard for how people bank and pay in Germany. We’re putting our cloud-first issuing technology and expertise behind that ambition, starting with a card customers can use the very moment they open an account. This partnership reinforces Enfuce’s proven ability to deliver at the scale and standard the world’s biggest banks demand.”

title: Payments Need an Operating System, Not Another Tool
summary:
Ask a Head of Payments how many systems they open to explain why approval rates dropped in Germany last Tuesday, and the answer is rarely fewer than four. A PSP dashboard, an acquirer portal, a fraud console, a finance spreadsheet. Each does its job. Together, they leave nobody in control.
That is the case for a payment operating system: one layer that runs the whole payment stack, rather than another product bolted onto it. Since we founded Corefy in 2018, I have watched teams solve connectivity again and again and still lose control of what happens after the connection. That gap is the next decision that separates payment teams who steer from those who react.
Most payment stacks grew by accident
Payment stacks are rarely planned. A second PSP gets added for redundancy, a local acquirer for a new market, a wallet because a product team asked for it, a fraud vendor after a bad quarter. Every decision made sense at the time, and the result is a stack that nobody has a full view of.
Our own research shows how common this is. In The State of Payment Maturity 2025, 58.5% of the 672 businesses assessed ran fragmented payments, with disconnected providers and tools. Only 11.7% reached the responsive or agile stages, where payments are managed as one adaptive system. Manual processing has almost disappeared (1.0%), and single-provider setups keep declining, so connecting to providers is no longer the hard part. The remaining gap is control across them.
Every new tool adds another silo
The reflex answer to fragmentation is to buy something: a routing tool, a reconciliation tool, a monitoring tool. Each purchase is rational. Each also brings an integration, a dashboard, and a data model to maintain. The routing tool does not know what reconciliation found. The analytics tool sees transactions after the fact and cannot change how the next one is processed.
I understand the best-of-breed argument, and for a team with a large platform engineering function it can work. The objection I hear most is, "we can wire these together ourselves." Many do. The cost appears later, when adding a provider in a new market touches five systems and takes two quarters of engineering time. A stack of tools records decisions made at different moments by different people. It has no way to make them together.
A payment operating system gives the stack one layer of control
An operating system does not replace the applications on a computer. It gives them shared resources, a common interface, and rules for who gets what. A payment operating system does the same for providers, methods, and data. Your PSPs and acquirers stay where they are, and the operating system sits above them.
In architectural terms, this is a payment hub architecture: providers connect to the hub once, and everything above it, from checkout to finance, talks to a single interface. Four layers define a payment infrastructure built this way:
Connectivity. One integration replaces a project per provider. Corefy's catalog holds 650+ connectors with standardized APIs, webhooks, and error handling, which means enabling a provider becomes configuration instead of a build.
Control. Routing & Cascading rules by BIN, geography, currency, risk, or provider performance decide where each transaction goes, then retry recoverable declines through the next eligible route. Payment managers change the logic themselves, without a ticket to engineering.
Data. Every transaction from every provider lands in one normalized record. Reconciliations match that record against provider statements and surface only the exceptions, so finance stops reviewing everything by hand.
Operations. Payments and payouts, roles, merchant hierarchies, and alerts run from the same place as acceptance, so one team sees the full money flow.
Concentrating control in one layer raises a fair question: does that create a new single point of failure and a new vendor lock-in? The risk is real, and the design answers it. Contracts, merchant accounts, and credentials stay with your providers. Corefy, for example, does not hold client funds. Insist that routing logic and transaction data remain exportable, and insist on failover inside the layer itself.
Three signs your stack has outgrown its tools
You do not need a formal audit to know where you stand. Check three things:
Adding a provider takes weeks of engineering instead of days of configuration.
Routing changes need a developer, so nobody changes them, and last year's rules still run.
Payments and finance disagree about last month's numbers, and settling the difference takes a spreadsheet and a meeting.
If two of the three sound familiar, you are managing integrations, not payments. That work belongs in a layer built for it.
Start by adding to the stack, not replacing it
The usual objection is risk: nobody wants to rip out a live stack. A payment operating system does not require a big-bang migration. Start with what is new. Put the next provider, the next market, or the next payment method on the operating system first. If you already process through a gateway or another orchestration platform and only lack connectors, Payment Bridge adds 650+ of them without migration or downtime.
Then move the routing logic for one market, then reconciliation. Old integrations retire on their own once nothing new depends on them. Founders building a payment business can follow the same path from the other side: a white-label foundation lets you launch on the operating system instead of writing one.
Run payments as a system
The data says the first problem is behind us. Manual processing is gone, and connectors are a commodity. What separates a payment team that steers from one that reacts is a single place where routing, data, and operations meet. That is what a payment operating system provides, and it is the standard I expect payment teams to hold themselves to over the next few years.
If you want to see what this looks like on your own stack, talk to the Corefy team. Bring your provider list and your most frustrating report. We will start there.

title: The Investment Hiding in Plain Sight
summary:
Every investment proposal arriving on a CFO's desk has to answer the same question: what is the return? Finance modernisation should be judged by the same standard. So the question, therefore, is what measurable return will an investment in modernising your finance function deliver.
The most compelling business cases are built on returns that begin to accrue from day one, and this is not a pipedream. Corpay’s research engaged with 300 UK CFOs and they agreed that finance modernisation can deliver this. Not eventually or after a multi-year transformation programme, but from the moment payment strategy begins to change.
Getting more from your modernisation: improving liquidity before it improves technology
Working capital is often discussed as though it’s created through borrowing. Yet some of the quickest gains come from changing how money leaves the business. Card-led payment strategies can extend payment timing, which means organisations retain cash for longer without disrupting supplier relationships. That is liquidity improvement with minimum impact on technology, straightforward implementation, and limited upfront investment.
Working capital is a strategic asset. Finance teams with greater liquidity can respond to opportunities quicker, manage unexpected costs more comfortably and approach investment decisions from a position of greater confidence. Unsurprisingly, 99% of the CFOs in our research said that additional working capital flexibility would be at least somewhat valuable but getting there requires a more deliberate approach to how payments are executed.
Every payment can be the beginning of value creation
Every payment has traditionally been treated as the end of a transaction. Increasingly, finance leaders are recognising it can also be the beginning of value creation.
When organisations consolidate qualifying spend onto card-based payments, they create the conditions for rebate income, creating a direct financial return on operational spending that would otherwise generate nothing beyond the transaction itself. When CFOs in our research were asked how they would reinvest a 1% rebate on qualifying spend, they prioritised automation, employee development and training.
Taken together, improved working capital and commercial card rebates can turn operational spending into a source of financial value. That value can then be reinvested in further modernisation. Payments become a commercial lever, with returns beginning from the first qualifying transaction and growing as more eligible spend moves onto card.
The capacity question: what is reclaimed time actually worth?
Earlier this year, we called this hidden operational burden the Manual Tax because every finance team pays it, whether it appears on a budget line or not. The hours absorbed by administration across expenses, invoices and supplier payments cost UK finance teams the equivalent of a working day per person, per week. 86% of finance teams are living with that reality right now, according to our research.
The next question is what that reclaimed capacity is actually worth to the business. When CFOs were asked how they would redeploy time if administrative workload were reduced by 25 to 50%, the answer was consistent: Forecasting, strategic planning and business partnering. These are the activities and work that define what a finance function can contribute to an organisation's overall performance.
Reducing that burden doesn’t require a full system replacement. Instead, it’s structuring spend at the point of payment rather than reconstructing it downstream. When transaction data is captured automatically, the reconciliation workload reduces significantly, control moves closer to the moment of spending, visibility improves in real time and finance teams recover capacity that can be directed toward higher-value work from the following week, not the following year.
Building the case for more working capital
I hope the examples I’ve provide show that finance modernisation does not have to begin with a large-scale and expensive transformation programme. The strongest business cases with immediate returns are often built through smaller, deliberate decisions that tackle less traditional finance functions.
Working capital flexibility and rebate income are all available to any organisation willing to take a more deliberate approach to how spend is authorised, executed and recorded. The returns are fast, measurable and more accessible than most CFOs assume.
For many organisations, that journey starts with payment strategy. Making modernisation pay is about making better decisions about how money moves through the business with as much attention on payment channels as other areas.

Before joining Cointelegraph, she spent more than a decade in senior leadership roles at major banking and insurance companies, including Allianz. Phase is building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, giving AI agents everything they need to operate autonomously, from accessing the open web and orchestrating AI models to performing computing tasks and making payments. These services run on Phase’s Layer 1 blockchain, powered by a decentralized network of everyday devices whose owners earn rewards for validating transactions and contributing connectivity and computing power. “AI agents are moving from answering questions to performing real tasks on our behalf, but the infrastructure they depend on was not built for autonomous systems. Phase is building an open, decentralized network that anyone can participate in. My focus is to bring this technology to developers and businesses worldwide and build the ecosystem needed to support the next generation of AI agents,” said Yana Prikhodchenko, co-founder and CEO of Phase. “Yana brings extensive leadership experience across media, technology and financial services, along with the operational expertise and industry relationships needed to take Phase into its next stage of growth. As we bring our technology to market, she will lead the company’s commercial development and global expansion,” said Kirill Eves, founder of Phase.   About Phase Phase is a technology company building the operating layer for the AI agent economy, with four integrated services that give AI agents everything they need to operate autonomously, from accessing the open web and orchestrating AI models to performing computing tasks and making payments. The platform runs on its own Layer 1 blockchain, powered by a decentralized network of everyday devices. Phase has received $45 million in funding from its founder, Kirill Eves. Phase Router intelligently directs requests across leading AI models to optimize quality, performance and cost. Phase Compute harnesses the processing power of devices across the network to run open-weight AI models, while on-chain settlement enables autonomous payments using stablecoins and PHASE, the network’s native token. Unlike most blockchain networks that require dedicated servers or token staking, Phase allows anyone to become a validator simply by downloading the app, without specialized hardware or upfront investment. Its reputation-based consensus and randomized validator selection secure the network and prevent control from concentrating in the hands of a few powerful operators. Phase rewards device owners with PHASE tokens for validating blocks and contributing connectivity and computing power, enabling millions of people to help build the AI economy and share in the value it creates. title: Alta Raises $80 Million to Build the Infrastructure for Global Onchain Finance
summary:
Alta, a financial infrastructure company building the foundation for the next generation of global finance, today announced it has raised $80 million in total funding, including a $47.5 million Series A round and $32.5 million in previous seed financing. The Series A was led by Index Ventures, with participation from GV (Google Ventures), Blackbird Ventures, Square Peg, and Capital 49.
Alta is building new institutional-grade blockchain infrastructure that enables financial assets and products to move instantly, globally, and programmatically. Unlike existing infrastructure built primarily for crypto-native applications, Alta is designed to meet the privacy, compliance, neutrality, and operational requirements of regulated financial institutions while supporting transactions across assets, chains, and jurisdictions. Its launch comes as regulatory clarity improves and institutional demand for tokenized finance accelerates.
“Existing blockchains aren’t designed for the privacy and compliance requirements of global financial institutions,” said Loong Wang, Co-Founder and CEO of Alta. “We’re taking a fundamentally different approach, building privacy, programmable compliance, and identity and authorization directly into the blockchain. This will enable money and assets to move instantly, globally, and securely, whether it’s a bank settling a transaction or an AI agent making a payment.”
Today’s global financial system is fragmented and still has many areas of inefficiency. Moving money across borders can take days, and institutions must maintain substantial cash buffers to ensure liquidity across jurisdictions and payment networks. An estimated $4 trillion is tied up in prefunded accounts globally. Alta is building a more efficient system, combining instant settlement with global payment connectivity, foreign exchange, and treasury management capabilities.
At the core of Alta’s technology is a new blockchain architecture built on recursive zero-knowledge cryptography. It enables institutions to keep balances, transactions, identities, and compliance policies private while verifying that transactions meet the required rules. Designed to work across assets, chains, and jurisdictions, Alta combines programmable compliance with the controls and scalability needed for institutional finance and agentic commerce.
“Technology alone won’t be enough to modernize global finance. Financial institutions need infrastructure they can trust, with clear controls over who they’re transacting with, where money can move, and how sensitive information is protected,” said Catherine Porter, Co-Founder and President of Alta. “As AI agents increasingly make financial decisions and execute transactions, that trust becomes even more critical. Privacy, compliance, and accountability just aren’t barriers to innovation – they’re what will allow it to scale.”
Leading financial platform Airwallex has chosen to build on Alta, connecting its global payments infrastructure with Alta’s blockchain technology. In addition to pay-ins and pay-outs via stablecoins, the collaboration will support connectivity to local fiat payment networks across 200 countries and 90 currencies. Alta is designed as neutral infrastructure that banks, payment providers, and other financial institutions can build on.
Alta’s first product will help businesses manage liquidity more efficiently and reduce cash buffers tied up in prefunded accounts. Built on tokenized assets, it will enable just-in-time funding, more efficient foreign exchange, and allow businesses to instantly move in and out of yield-bearing tokenized assets, maximizing the interest earned on otherwise idle capital.
“With the rise of agentic banking and programmable payments, stablecoins are becoming an important vector for settlement. Financial institutions need blockchain infrastructure that is private, neutral, regulated, and connected to global fiat rails. Alta is building exactly that,” said Jack Zhang, Co-Founder of Alta and Co-Founder/CEO of Airwallex. “We’re proud to be an early design partner and help Alta deliver onchain finance at institutional scale.”
Backed by Leading Global Investors
Alta’s investors bring together expertise across financial technology, enterprise infrastructure, and blockchain innovation.
“Loong is the sort of technologist you only meet a few times in a career. After a major fintech exit from his first company, he went on to run the largest supercomputing calculation in history at its time, then discovered a cancer drug now in human trials. With Catherine’s exceptional track record of bringing industry leaders to the table and Jack’s understanding of the problem space, this is a team we had to back,” said Jan Hammer, Partner at Index Ventures.
“The Alta founders have successfully built and scaled multi-billion-dollar technology and financial infrastructure businesses, and understand how to de-risk complex institutional execution. We have been impressed with their combination of deep-tech blockchain engineering, institutional go-to-market knowledge, and vision for scale, and we look forward to supporting them in their mission to reimagine financial infrastructure at its core,” said Tom Hulme, Managing Partner at GV.
“Stablecoins solved speed. Alta is solving trust, with privacy by default and compliance written into the settlement itself, so the institutions that hold the world’s money can finally use them. We’ve known Loong and Jack for years, and watching two of Melbourne’s best join forces, with Airwallex anchoring Alta from day one, is the kind of moment this job is for. Catherine is more than their match. She built the enterprise stablecoin playbook at Meta before most people knew one existed, and together she and Loong are the most complete founding team we’ve seen in a long time,” said Michael Tolo, General Partner with Blackbird Ventures.
“We are thrilled to be participating in Alta’s Series A. Alta brings a combination of a world class team with incredible domain expertise solving an important problem at exactly the right time. We are so excited to have the opportunity to back Loong and Catherine and their team early in their journey,” said Paul Bassat, Co-Founder and Partner at Square Peg.
“We have backed Alta since its founding, and what stands out about this team is how fast they turn conviction into working infrastructure. Global finance won’t move onchain without institutional-grade readiness, and that’s exactly what Alta is demonstrating, one partner at a time,” said Chris Cheng, Managing Director at Capital 49.
The new funding will support continued development of Alta’s blockchain infrastructure, expansion of its institutional partnerships and global financial connectivity, and growth of its engineering and compliance teams.
